div.head: II Cn 39
div.ab: Gyf hwa weofodþen afylle, sy he utlah wið God ⁊ wið men, butan he þurh wræcsið þe deoppor gebete, ⁊ eac wið ða mægðe; oððe geladige hine mid werlade.
Gif hwa wefodþén afylle, sy he utlah wið God ⁊ wið men, buton he þurh wrecsyð þe deoppor gebete, ⁊ eac wið þa mægðe; oððe geladige hine mid werlade.
Si quis altaris ministrum occidat, útlaga sit erga Deum et homines, nisi dignis satisfactionibus ueros penitentię fructus ostendat et erga parentes eius emendet; uel wéralada se adlegiet.
Gif hwa preost ofslea. Gyf hwa weofodðegen afylle, sy he utlaga wið God ⁊ wið men, buton he ðurh wrecsið ðe deoppor gebete ⁊ eac wið ða mægða, oððe ladige mid werlade.
Gyf hwa weofodþen afylle, sy he utlah wið God and wið men, butan he þurh wræcsið þe deoppor gebete, and eac wið ða mægðe; oððe geladige hine mid werlade.

(Wenn jemand einen Priester erschlägt. B) Wenn einer einen Altardiener tödtet, sei er friedlos in Kirche und Staat, ausser wenn er um so tiefer durch elende Verbannungspilgerfahrt, und ebenfalls gegenüber der Sippe [des Erschlagenen], büsst — oder er reinige sich durch Eid [so hoch wie dessen] Wergeld —;

(If anyone kills a priest. B) If anyone kills a servant of the altar, let him be an outlaw before God and men, unless he atones all the more deeply by a pilgrimage of exile, and also [makes amends] to the kindred [of the slain] — or let him clear himself by an oath [to the amount of the victim's] wergild —;

If anyone slay a priest. If anyone slays a minister of the altar, he shall be both excommunicated and outlawed, unless he make amends to the best of his ability by pilgrimage, and likewise by [the payment of compensation] to the kin [of the slain man], or else he shall clear himself by an oath equal in value to his wergeld.

If anyone slays a minister of the altar, he is to be an outlaw before God and men, unless he atone for it very deeply, by pilgrimage and also towards the kindred, or clear himself by an oath equal to the wergild.

If anyone kills a minister of the altar, he shall be excommunicated and outlawed, unless he repents all the more sincerely by making pilgrimage and also by paying compensation to his victim’s family; or he may exonerate himself by an oath equal to the value of his wergild.
